description: A content type schema defines the structural contract for all CMS content types: their fields, types, validation rules, and relationships — and must be internally consistent before any content can be created.

rules.description: A content-type-schema.spec.json file must exist in the artifact directory and must be valid JSON with a non-empty types array.
Every content type must have a unique string id. Duplicate IDs cause CMS schema conflicts that silently overwrite each other.
Every content type must have at least one required:true field. A fully optional type cannot enforce content quality or integrity.
Every field of type 'slug' must declare unique:true. Non-unique slugs produce duplicate URLs, breaking routing and SEO.
Every reference field must declare referenceTo pointing to a content type ID that exists in the same schema. Dangling references crash CMS rendering.
Content types must not form circular reference chains (A → B → A) unless explicitly marked bidirectional:true. Unintended cycles cause infinite CMS query loops.
Every image field must explicitly declare altRequired:true or altRequired:false. Undeclared alt text policy causes inconsistent a11y enforcement across content authors.
All field names must follow camelCase convention. Inconsistent naming breaks CMS API field mapping and frontend prop alignment.
